data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: Use of Web Measurement and Customization Technologies
extract_result.opi: Office of the Chief Information Officer

USDA Chief Privacy Officer and Agency Privacy Act Officers

all agency program managers, IT personnel, and contractors

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes guidance for the use of web measurement and customization technologies and the associated privacy requirements for public-facing and third-party websites and applications owned or operated on behalf of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).
policy_statements.target: use of web measurement and customization technologies and the associated privacy requirements for public-facing and third-party websites and applications owned or operated on behalf of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA)

policy_statements.source_text: This directive does not apply to internal agency activities (such as intranets, applications, or interactions not involving the public) or to activities that are part of authorized law enforcement, national security, or intelligence activities.
policy_statements.target: internal agency activities (such as intranets, applications, or interactions not involving the public)

policy_statements.source_text: This policy adheres to the guidance identified in the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 3 identified in the table below.
policy_statements.target: guidance identified in the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 3
cross_references: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 3

policy_statements.source_text: Unless otherwise specified, this directive applies to all USDA agency and staff office personnel, including non-Government personnel (e.g., contractors, interns, and partners) authorized to use USDA web and application resources, including third-party websites, for official USDA purposes.
policy_statements.target: all USDA agency and staff office personnel, including non-Government personnel (e.g., contractors, interns, and partners) authorized to use USDA web and application resources, including third-party websites, for official USDA purposes

policy_statements.source_text: This policy supersedes Departmental Manual (DM) 3515-001, Collection of Web Page Cookies & Privacy Requirements, dated August 19, 2004.
policy_statements.target: Departmental Manual (DM) 3515-001, Collection of Web Page Cookies & Privacy Requirements
cross_references: Departmental Manual (DM) 3515-001, Collection of Web Page Cookies & Privacy Requirements, dated August 19, 2004

policy_statements.source_text: The title of this policy has been changed to reflect changes in the terminology used by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB).

OMB Memorandum M-10-22, Guidance for Online Use of Web Measurement and Customization Technologies rescinds OMB Memorandum M-00-13, Privacy Policies and Data Collection on Federal Websites and the following specified sections in OMB Memorandum M-03-22, OMB Guidance for Implementing the Privacy Provisions of the E-Government Act of 2002: Section III(D)(2)(v) concerning tracking and customization activities, and Section VII(B) regarding the reporting of tracking technologies.
cross_references: OMB Memorandum M-10-22, Guidance for Online Use of Web Measurement and Customization Technologies
OMB Memorandum M-00-13, Privacy Policies and Data Collection on Federal Websites
OMB Memorandum M-03-22, OMB Guidance for Implementing the Privacy Provisions of the E-Government Act of 2002

policy_statements.source_text: The free flow of information between the government and the public is essential in a democratic society.
However, the individual’s right to privacy must be protected in the Federal Government’s information activities involving personal information.
policy_statements.target: individual’s right to privacy

policy_statements.source_text: The Federal Government has established guidelines for the use of web measurement and customization technologies and to enable the useful functioning of federal websites while protecting individual privacy.

Agencies may use web measurement and customization technologies (e.g., persistent cookies, web analytics, etc.) for the purpose of improving Federal services online through conducting measurement and analysis of usage or through customization of the user’s experience.
policy_statements.target: web measurement and customization technologies

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies may not use web measurement and customization technologies to:
track user individual-level activity on the Internet outside of the website or application from which the technology originates;
policy_statements.target: user individual-level activity on the Internet outside of the website or application from which the technology originates

policy_statements.source_text: share the data obtained through such technologies, without the user’s explicit consent, with other departments or agencies;
policy_statements.target: data obtained through such technologies

policy_statements.source_text: cross-reference, without the user’s explicit consent, any data gathered from web measurement and customization technologies against PII to determine individual-level online activity;
policy_statements.target: any data gathered from web measurement and customization technologies

policy_statements.source_text: collect PII without the user’s explicit consent in any fashion; or
policy_statements.target: PII

policy_statements.source_text: for any like usages so designated by OMB.
policy_statements.target: any like usages so designated by OMB

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will only collect or create information necessary for the proper performance of the agency’s functions and which has practical utility.
policy_statements.target: information necessary for the proper performance of the agency’s functions and which has practical utility
conditions: necessary for the proper performance of the agency’s functions and which has practical utility

policy_statements.source_text: Each agency/mission area will consider the effects of their actions on the privacy rights of individuals, and ensure that appropriate legal and technical safeguards are implemented.
policy_statements.target: effects of their actions on the privacy rights of individuals

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies must exercise care to ensure that they comply with OMB's privacy policies cited in Appendix B of this document and the requirements outlined in the Privacy Act of 1974.
policy_statements.target: OMB's privacy policies cited in Appendix B of this document and the requirements outlined in the Privacy Act of 1974

policy_statements.source_text: The Privacy Act allows individuals to access documents maintained in a Privacy Act system of records and to request amendments to the records.
policy_statements.target: individuals

policy_statements.source_text: Visitors to a USDA website must receive clear and conspicuous notification in the Department’s privacy notice regarding the use of technologies for collecting an individual's information and how that information will be used.
policy_statements.target: Visitors to a USDA website

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will comply with the standards set forth in the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998 (COPPA) with respect to the collection of personal information directed at children.
policy_statements.target: standards set forth in the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998 (COPPA)
cross_references: Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998 (COPPA)

policy_statements.source_text: USDA will not knowingly contact or collect personal information or solicit information of any kind for children under the age of 13.
policy_statements.target: personal information

policy_statements.source_text: It is possible that by fraud or deception we may receive information pertaining to children under the age of 13.
If such actions are detected, the USDA Chief Privacy Officer should be notified via the Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Hotline and the information reviewed for further action.
policy_statements.target: USDA Chief Privacy Officer

policy_statements.source_text: OMB M-10-22 defines tiers for authorized use of web measurement and customization technologies.
policy_statements.target: tiers for authorized use of web measurement and customization technologies

policy_statements.source_text: Tier 1 – single session.
This tier encompasses any use of single session web measurement and customization technologies.
policy_statements.target: any use of single session web measurement and customization technologies

policy_statements.source_text: Tier 2 – multi-session without PII.

This tier encompasses any use of multi-session web measurement and customization technologies when no PII is collected (including when the agency is unable to identify an individual as a result of its use of such technologies).
policy_statements.target: any use of multi-session web measurement and customization technologies
conditions: when no PII is collected (including when the agency is unable to identify an individual as a result of its use of such technologies)

policy_statements.source_text: Tier 3 – multi-session with PII.

This tier encompasses any use of multi-session web measurement and customization technologies when PII is collected (including when the agency is able to identify an individual as a result of its use of such technologies).
policy_statements.target: any use of multi-session web measurement and customization technologies
conditions: when PII is collected (including when the agency is able to identify an individual as a result of its use of such technologies)

policy_statements.source_text: More detailed information pertaining to usage tiers and associated privacy requirements can be found in OMB M-10-22, Attachments 1 and 2.

Before an agency uses a third-party website or application to engage with the public, the agency must follow the process identified in DR 1495-001, New Media Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities, which requires evaluation by the Office of Communications (OC) and Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) prior to use and implementation of the third-party site.
policy_statements.target: process identified in DR 1495-001, New Media Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
conditions: Before an agency uses a third-party website or application to engage with the public
cross_references: DR 1495-001, New Media Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities

policy_statements.source_text: The agency shall, at a minimum, review the third-party’s privacy policy quarterly to confirm appropriateness and reassess risk.
policy_statements.target: third-party’s privacy policy

policy_statements.source_text: Before an agency uses a third-party website or application to engage with the public, the agency must exercise due diligence to determine whether the third-party’s website or application contains links to sites that may provide content not supported or endorsed by the Department.
conditions: Before an agency uses a third-party website or application to engage with the public

policy_statements.source_text: The agency shall, at a minimum, review the third-party's website quarterly to confirm appropriateness.
policy_statements.target: third-party's website

policy_statements.source_text: If an agency posts a link that leads to a third-party website or any other location that is not part of an official government domain, a statement adjacent to the link or visual alert must be provided to notify the user that they are being directed to a non-government website that may have different privacy policies from those of the agency's official website.
policy_statements.target: statement adjacent to the link or visual alert
conditions: If an agency posts a link that leads to a third-party website or any other location that is not part of an official government domain

policy_statements.source_text: Visual alerts must comply with federal regulations and policies.
policy_statements.target: federal regulations and policies

policy_statements.source_text: USDA agencies using a third-party website or application for content placement that is not part of an official government domain must ensure that appropriate USDA branding is applied to distinguish the agency's activities from those of non-government entities.
policy_statements.target: appropriate USDA branding
conditions: using a third-party website or application for content placement that is not part of an official government domain

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies utilizing a third-party service to solicit feedback must also provide an alternative government e-mail address where users can also send feedback.
policy_statements.target: alternative government e-mail address
conditions: utilizing a third-party service to solicit feedback

policy_statements.source_text: Information collected through an agency's use of a third-party website or application must only collect the information “...necessary for the proper performance of agency functions and which has practical utility.”1
If PII is collected, the agency shall collect only the minimum necessary to accomplish a purpose required by statute, regulation, or executive order.
policy_statements.target: only the minimum necessary to accomplish a purpose required by statute, regulation, or executive order

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies are required to perform a PIA whenever the use of a third-party website or application makes PII available to the agency.
policy_statements.target: PIA
conditions: whenever the use of a third-party website or application makes PII available to the agency

policy_statements.source_text: The PIA shall describe:
The specific purpose of the agency’s use of the third-party website or application;
Any PII that is likely to become available to the agency through public use of the third-party website or application;
The agency’s intended or expected use of PII;
With whom the agency will share PII;
Whether and how the agency will maintain PII, and for how long;
How the agency will secure PII that it uses or maintains;
What other privacy risks exist and how the agency will mitigate those risks; and
Whether the agency’s activities will create or modify a “system of records” under the Privacy Act.
In general, an agency’s use of a third-party website or application shall be covered in a single, separate PIA.
policy_statements.target: agency’s use of a third-party website or application

policy_statements.source_text: However, an agency may prepare one PIA to cover multiple websites or applications that are functionally comparable, as long as the agency’s practices are substantially similar across each website and application.
policy_statements.target: one PIA
conditions: as long as the agency’s practices are substantially similar across each website and application

policy_statements.source_text: If an agency’s use of a website or application raises distinct privacy risks, the agency shall prepare a PIA that is exclusive to that website or application.
policy_statements.target: PIA that is exclusive to that website or application
conditions: If an agency’s use of a website or application raises distinct privacy risks

policy_statements.source_text: If the agency’s use of a website or application results in the ability to retrieve PII, the agency shall comply with the system of records notice requirement of the Privacy Act.
policy_statements.target: system of records notice requirement of the Privacy Act
conditions: If the agency’s use of a website or application results in the ability to retrieve PII

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA agencies and staff offices are required to conform to the policy; however, in the event that a policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated, agencies may submit a waiver request.
policy_statements.target: waiver request
conditions: in the event that a policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated

policy_statements.source_text: The waiver request must explain the reason for the request, identify compensating controls/actions that meet the intent of the policy, and identify how the compensating control/action provides a similar or greater level of defense or compliance than the policy requirement.
policy_statements.target: reason for the request

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and staff offices will submit all policy waiver requests directly to the Associate Chief Information Officer (ACIO) for Cyber Policy and Oversight (CPO) for review and decision.
policy_statements.target: all policy waiver requests

policy_statements.source_text: Unless otherwise specified, agencies must review and renew approved policy waivers every fiscal year.
policy_statements.target: approved policy waivers

policy_statements.source_text: Approved waivers must be recorded and tracked as a Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) item in the Department’s Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) data management and reporting tool.
policy_statements.target: Approved waivers

policy_statements.source_text: CPO will monitor all approved waivers.
policy_statements.target: all approved waivers

policy_statements.source_text: This DR may be further shaped by other USDA regulations and manuals that contain clarifying procedures.
USDA Departmental regulations and manuals can be found at: http://www.ocio.usda.gov/directives/index.html.
Additional references can also be found in Appendix B of this directive.
The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Director, Office of Communications will:
Ensure that USDA agencies/mission areas comply with current Federal and OMB guidance with regard to the use of web measurement and customization technologies and protection of PII; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Director, Office of Communications
policy_statements.target: USDA agencies/mission areas

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that information resulting from the annual web measurement and customization technology system/procedure reviews are posted on the agency’s “USDA.gov/open” page and a public feedback mechanism established.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Director, Office of Communications
policy_statements.target: information resulting from the annual web measurement and customization technology system/procedure reviews

policy_statements.source_text: The Associate CIO for Cyber Policy and Oversight (ACIO-CPO) will:
Publish minimum requirements identifying the Department’s approach to OMB and other relevant Federal agency-issued web measurement and customization technologies and privacy guidance;
policy_statements.actor_name: Associate CIO for Cyber Policy and Oversight (ACIO-CPO)
policy_statements.target: minimum requirements identifying the Department’s approach to OMB and other relevant Federal agency-issued web measurement and customization technologies and privacy guidance

policy_statements.source_text: Issue direction to cease operating websites if the agency/mission area or contractor is not in compliance with the policies identified in this directive and does not correct the problem in a timely manner (within 2 working days).
policy_statements.actor_name: Associate CIO for Cyber Policy and Oversight (ACIO-CPO)
policy_statements.target: direction to cease operating websites
conditions: if the agency/mission area or contractor is not in compliance with the policies identified in this directive and does not correct the problem in a timely manner (within 2 working days)

policy_statements.source_text: Review and render decision on waivers to the guidance established in this policy.
policy_statements.actor_name: Associate CIO for Cyber Policy and Oversight (ACIO-CPO)
policy_statements.target: waivers to the guidance established in this policy

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Privacy Officer and Agency Privacy Act Officers will:
Ensure that USDA agencies/mission areas and contractors comply with the requirements of the Privacy Act and COPPA with regard to the collection and use of personal information.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Chief Privacy Officer and Agency Privacy Act Officers
policy_statements.target: USDA agencies/mission areas and contractors

policy_statements.source_text: At a minimum, annually review the online privacy notice on the www.USDA.gov page to ensure the notice provides the public with the most current guidance and information.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Chief Privacy Officer and Agency Privacy Act Officers
policy_statements.target: online privacy notice on the www.USDA.gov page

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of the Inspector General (OIG) will:
Incorporate a review of applicable requirements concerning the use of web measurement and customization technologies and posting of privacy notices in their audit of USDA websites, as appropriate.
policy_statements.target: review of applicable requirements concerning the use of web measurement and customization technologies and posting of privacy notices

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of the General Counsel (OGC) will:

The free flow of information between the government and the public is essential in a democratic society.
However, the individual’s right to privacy must be protected in the Federal Government’s information activities involving personal information.

The Federal Government has established guidelines for the use of web measurement and customization technologies and to enable the useful functioning of federal websites while protecting individual privacy.

Agencies may use web measurement and customization technologies (e.g., persistent cookies, web analytics, etc.) for the purpose of improving Federal services online through conducting measurement and analysis of usage or through customization of the user’s experience.
Agencies may not use web measurement and customization technologies to:
track user individual-level activity on the Internet outside of the website or application from which the technology originates;
user individual-level activity on the Internet outside of the website or application from which the technology originates
share the data obtained through such technologies, without the user’s explicit consent, with other departments or agencies;
cross-reference, without the user’s explicit consent, any data gathered from web measurement and customization technologies against PII to determine individual-level online activity;
any data gathered from web measurement and customization technologies
collect PII without the user’s explicit consent in any fashion; or
for any like usages so designated by OMB.
any like usages so designated by OMB
Agencies will only collect or create information necessary for the proper performance of the agency’s functions and which has practical utility.
information necessary for the proper performance of the agency’s functions and which has practical utility
necessary for the proper performance of the agency’s functions and which has practical utility
Each agency/mission area will consider the effects of their actions on the privacy rights of individuals, and ensure that appropriate legal and technical safeguards are implemented.
effects of their actions on the privacy rights of individuals
Agencies must exercise care to ensure that they comply with OMB's privacy policies cited in Appendix B of this document and the requirements outlined in the Privacy Act of 1974.

The Privacy Act allows individuals to access documents maintained in a Privacy Act system of records and to request amendments to the records.

Visitors to a USDA website must receive clear and conspicuous notification in the Department’s privacy notice regarding the use of technologies for collecting an individual's information and how that information will be used.
Agencies will comply with the standards set forth in the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998 (COPPA) with respect to the collection of personal information directed at children.

USDA will not knowingly contact or collect personal information or solicit information of any kind for children under the age of 13.
It is possible that by fraud or deception we may receive information pertaining to children under the age of 13.
If such actions are detected, the USDA Chief Privacy Officer should be notified via the Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Hotline and the information reviewed for further action.

The waiver request must explain the reason for the request, identify compensating controls/actions that meet the intent of the policy, and identify how the compensating control/action provides a similar or greater level of defense or compliance than the policy requirement.
Agencies and staff offices will submit all policy waiver requests directly to the Associate Chief Information Officer (ACIO) for Cyber Policy and Oversight (CPO) for review and decision.
Unless otherwise specified, agencies must review and renew approved policy waivers every fiscal year.
